blocks.text: When two different halogens react with each other, interhalogen compounds are formed. They can be assigned general compositions as XX ′ , XX3 ′, XX5 ′ and XX7 ′ where X is halogen of larger size and X ′ of smaller size and X is more electropositive than X ′. As the ratio between radii of X and X ′ increases, the number of atoms per molecule also increases. Thus, iodine (VII) fluoride should have maximum number of atoms as the ratio of radii between I and F should be maximum. That is why its formula is IF7 (having maximum number of atoms).

The interhalogen compounds can be prepared by the direct combination or by the action of halogen on lower interhalogen compounds. The product formed depends upon some specific conditions, For example,
